```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Fokkink_2022_immunoglobulin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Fokkink_2022_immunoglobulin"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-022-01136-z> (open access; the
  Electronic Supplementary Material contains the final NONMEM control stream)

# Population

The model-building cohort combined 177 patients with Guillain-Barre syndrome
(GBS) from two Dutch GBS Study Group randomised trials -- IVIg versus plasma
exchange, and IVIg with or without intravenous methylprednisolone (500 mg/day
for 5 days) -- with 15 patients with stable chronic inflammatory demyelinating
polyneuropathy (CIDP) on IVIg maintenance, who supplied samples shortly after
infusion. GBS patients were unable to walk independently at entry and all
received IVIg 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 consecutive days (Gammagard S/D). The GBS
cohort (Fokkink 2022 Table 1) had mean age 53 years (range 5-89), mean weight
72 kg (range 18-122), 57% male, mean GBS disability score (GBS-DS) 4.1 at
nadir, 25% mechanically ventilated and 34% treated with methylprednisolone.
Total serum IgG was measured by turbidimetry (589 GBS samples, 222 CIDP
samples). The model was externally validated in 177 good-prognosis patients of
the SID-GBS trial.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Fokkink_2022_immunoglobulin")()$population`.

# Source trace

The per-parameter origin is recorded as an in-file comment next to each
`ini()` entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Fokkink_2022_immunoglobulin.R`.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Two-compartment IV model, elimination from central | -- | Results 3.1.1; Fig. 1; ESM control stream `ADVAN3 TRANS4` |
| Total IgG = IVIg-derived + CBAS | -- | Methods 2.3.1; ESM `$ERROR` `FTOT = F + CBAS` |
| `lcl` (CL, L/day per 70 kg) | 0.28 | Table 2, final model |
| `lvc` (V1, L) | 2.87 | Table 2, final model |
| `lq` (Q, L/day) | 0.25 | Table 2, final model |
| `lvp` (V2, L) | 2.65 | Table 2, final model |
| `e_wt_cl_q` | 0.75 (fixed) | Results 3.1.1; ESM `THETA(6)` FIX |
| `e_wt_vc_vp` | 1 (fixed) | Results 3.1.1; ESM `THETA(7)` FIX |
| `lbl_igg` (CBAS, g/L, CIDP) | 15.90 | Table 2, final model |
| `e_dis_gbs_bl_igg` | 0.65 | Table 2 'Disease type (if GBS)'; Methods 2.3.1 equation |
| `e_conmed_methylprednisolone_cl` | 1.31 | Table 2; Results 3.1.2 |
| `e_score_gbs_disability_34_cl` | 1.22 | Table 2; Results 3.1.2 |
| `e_score_gbs_disability_5_cl` | 1.83 | Table 2; Results 3.1.2 |
| GBS-DS grouping 0-2 / 3-4 / 5 | -- | Results 3.1.2; ESM `FSCORE` block |
| `etalcl` | 49.9% CV | Table 2 IIV |
| `etalbl_igg` | 23.1% CV | Table 2 IIV |
| `propSd` | 0.12 | Table 2 residual error; ESM `$ERROR` |

# Simulation of the paper's Figure 4 scenarios

Figure 4 of the paper simulates a 75 kg patient with GBS receiving 0.4 g/kg
IVIg as a 2-hour infusion each day for 5 days. The reference scenario is a
GBS-DS of 4 without methylprednisolone; panels B-D vary the disability score,
add methylprednisolone, and change the regimen. Each scenario below has 200
virtual patients with between-subject variability on CL and baseline IgG.

```{r scenarios}
mod <- readModelDb("Fokkink_2022_immunoglobulin")

scenarios <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario,                  ~score, ~mp, ~ndays, ~dose_kg,
  "GBS-DS 0-2",                   2,   0,      5,      0.4,
  "GBS-DS 3-4",                   4,   0,      5,      0.4,
  "GBS-DS 5",                     5,   0,      5,      0.4,
  "GBS-DS 4 + methylpred.",       4,   1,      5,      0.4,
  "0.4 g/kg/day x 6 days",        4,   0,      6,      0.4,
  "0.4 g/kg/day x 3 days",        4,   0,      3,      0.4,
  "1 g/kg/day x 2 days",          4,   0,      2,      1.0
) |>
  mutate(scenario = factor(scenario, levels = scenario))

n_per_arm <- 200
wt <- 75
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 7, by = 0.25), seq(7, 42, by = 1))))

make_arm <- function(i) {
  s <- scenarios[i, ]
  ids <- (i - 1) * n_per_arm + seq_len(n_per_arm)
  dose <- expand.grid(id = ids, day = seq_len(s$ndays) - 1) |>
    transmute(
      id, time = day, amt = s$dose_kg * wt, rate = s$dose_kg * wt / (2 / 24),
      evid = 1L, cmt = "central"
    )
  obs <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    mutate(
      scenario = s$scenario, WT = wt, SCORE_GBS_DISABILITY = s$score,
      CONMED_METHYLPREDNISOLONE = s$mp, DIS_GBS = 1L
    )
}
events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(scenarios)), make_arm)) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20220704)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod, events,
  keep = "scenario", returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  mutate(delta_igg = Cc - bl_igg)
```

```{r figure4, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
sim |>
  group_by(scenario, time) |>
  summarise(
    med = median(Cc), lo = quantile(Cc, 0.05), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 14, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~scenario, ncol = 4) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after start of IVIg (days)", y = "Total serum IgG (g/L)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Fokkink 2022: median and 90% interval."
  )
```

# Target attainment at two weeks

The paper's pharmacodynamic target is an increase of total IgG over baseline
(delta IgG) above 7.3 g/L at 2 weeks. In this model delta IgG is the
IVIg-derived concentration `central / vc`, so the baseline cancels and only the
clearance random effect matters. Because delta IgG at day 14 falls
monotonically as clearance rises, the attainment probability is exact:
find the `etalcl` at which a typical patient sits on the 7.3 g/L target, then
evaluate the normal distribution function at that threshold. This gives a
reference that does not depend on the random seed. The 200-patient simulation
from the previous section is shown next to it.

```{r target-exact}
ui <- suppressMessages(rxode2::rxode(mod))
typ <- suppressMessages(rxode2::zeroRe(ui))
omega_cl <- sqrt(ui$omega["etalcl", "etalcl"])
lcl0 <- ui$theta[["lcl"]]

delta_day14 <- function(eta, score, mp, ndays, dose_kg) {
  ev <- data.frame(
    id = 1, time = c(seq_len(ndays) - 1, 14),
    amt = c(rep(dose_kg * wt, ndays), 0),
    rate = c(rep(dose_kg * wt / (2 / 24), ndays), 0),
    evid = c(rep(1L, ndays), 0L), cmt = "central",
    WT = wt, SCORE_GBS_DISABILITY = score,
    CONMED_METHYLPREDNISOLONE = mp, DIS_GBS = 1L
  )
  s <- suppressMessages(rxode2::rxSolve(
    typ, ev,
    params = c(lcl = lcl0 + eta), returnType = "data.frame"
  ))
  s$Cc[s$time == 14] - s$bl_igg[s$time == 14]
}

exact_pta <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(scenarios)), function(i) {
  s <- scenarios[i, ]
  eta_star <- uniroot(
    function(e) delta_day14(e, s$score, s$mp, s$ndays, s$dose_kg) - 7.3,
    c(-3, 3)
  )$root
  100 * pnorm(eta_star / omega_cl)
}, numeric(1))

sim_pta <- sim |>
  filter(time == 14) |>
  group_by(scenario) |>
  summarise(sim = 100 * mean(delta_igg > 7.3), .groups = "drop")

pta <- scenarios |>
  select(scenario) |>
  mutate(
    published = c(74, 63, 33, 43, 74, 12, 54),
    exact = exact_pta
  ) |>
  left_join(sim_pta, by = "scenario") |>
  mutate(diff = exact - published)

pta |>
  mutate(across(c(exact, sim, diff), \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Scenario" = scenario,
    "Published (%)" = published,
    "Model, exact (%)" = exact,
    "Model, 200 simulated (%)" = sim,
    "Exact - published (points)" = diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Probability of delta IgG > 7.3 g/L at day 14 (Fokkink 2022 Results 3.2 and Figure 4).")

# The exact column is deterministic (no random draws), so a tight bound holds
# across rxode2 builds. The covariate ordering checks the direction of the
# GBS-DS and methylprednisolone effects and the regimen ranking.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(pta$diff) < 8),
  pta$exact[1] > pta$exact[2], pta$exact[2] > pta$exact[3],
  pta$exact[4] < pta$exact[2],
  pta$exact[5] > pta$exact[7], pta$exact[7] > pta$exact[6]
)
```

The exact attainment probabilities land within 5 percentage points of the
paper's Monte Carlo values (n = 1000 per scenario) for six of the seven
scenarios, and every covariate and regimen effect points the same way. The
largest gap is the 3-day regimen (about 18% versus the published 12%); the
paper does not say whether its simulated delta IgG included residual error or
how the baseline was subtracted, which matters most for a regimen whose typical
patient sits just below the target.

# Non-compartmental analysis

The paper reports no NCA. For completeness, PKNCA is run on the IVIg-derived
concentration (total IgG minus the individual endogenous baseline) for the
standard 5-day regimen in each GBS-DS group, over the 42-day simulation.

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- sim |>
  filter(scenario %in% c("GBS-DS 0-2", "GBS-DS 3-4", "GBS-DS 5")) |>
  filter(!is.na(delta_igg)) |>
  transmute(id, time, conc = delta_igg, treatment = as.character(scenario))

nca_dose <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1, scenario %in% c("GBS-DS 0-2", "GBS-DS 3-4", "GBS-DS 5")) |>
  transmute(id, time, amt, treatment = as.character(scenario))

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, conc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = 42,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_summary <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast", "half.life")) |>
  group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = signif(median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), 3), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)

nca_summary |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "GBS-DS group" = treatment,
    "Cmax (g/L)" = cmax,
    "Tmax (day)" = tmax,
    "AUC0-42 (g*day/L)" = auclast,
    "t1/2 (day)" = half.life
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median NCA of IVIg-derived IgG, 0.4 g/kg/day x 5 days, 75 kg.")
```

Clearance rises with disease severity, so AUC falls from the 0-2 group to the
GBS-DS 5 group while Cmax, which is governed by the central volume, changes
much less.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **CIDP clearance factor not encoded.** The control stream in the Electronic
  Supplementary Material estimates a separate multiplicative factor on CL for
  the CIDP patients (`THETA(10)`, GBS-DS coded -99), but the paper does not
  report its value. The model therefore applies the reference clearance to
  CIDP subjects (`DIS_GBS = 0` with `SCORE_GBS_DISABILITY` in 0-2). The CIDP
  baseline IgG (15.9 g/L) is reported and encoded. The model is intended for
  GBS; CIDP predictions of clearance are not supported by the paper.
* **IIV covariance not encoded.** The control stream uses an `OMEGA BLOCK(2)`
  on CL and CBAS, but only the two variances are reported, so the etas are
  independent.
* **IIV scale.** Table 2 reports IIV as a percentage, which is read as a CV:
  omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2). The target-attainment comparison above does not
  separate this from omega = CV (the two differ by about 6% on the SD scale).
* **GBS-DS grouping.** The score enters as the raw 0-6 value and is grouped
  in `model()` exactly as the paper and control stream group it. A score of 6
  (death) was disregarded by the authors and receives no CL factor.
* **Time units.** The control stream ran in hours; Table 2 reports CL and Q in
  L/day, so the model runs in days.
* **Peripheral compartment.** `peripheral1` carries the IVIg-derived IgG
  distributing outside the central (vascular) space; the paper does not
  identify the tissue.
